keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Westphalia shape begins in 1809, but the page says the kingdom 'existed from 1807 to 1813' (Treaty of Tilsit 7 July 1807, constitution adopted 7 December 1807). The page gives areas only from 1809 (37,883 km2), so the 1809 shape is extended back with that caveat.

43,140 km2 for 1809-1810 against the infobox 37,883 km2 (1809; ratio 1.14) and 63,652 km2 (1810; ratio 0.68), both inside a factor of two. The 1810 infobox figure includes departments (Nord, Niederelbe, Aller) that the shape does not; the ledger carries them (the 1810 gain /ledger/7 now covers Aller, Nord and Niederelbe, and the December 1810 loss returns the last two). The shape already covers the city of Hanover, so the 1810 Aller entry adds nothing to the cells there. Includes Osnabrück (the Weser department, 1807-1810).

38,231 km2 for 1811 against the infobox 45,427 km2 (1812; ratio 0.84). The shape no longer covers Osnabrück, which matches the page's department table: Weser (Osnabrück) 1807-1810, replaced by Aller (Hanover) 1810-1813.
Same shape as 1811 (38,231 km2) held to the kingdom's end; the page records no territorial change in 1811-1813 until the October 1813 collapse. Infobox 1812: 45,427 km2 (ratio 0.84).

region.text: Cassel, the capital; the kingdom 'created in 1807 from territories ceded by Prussia in the Peace of Tilsit, plus Hanover, Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, and Hesse'

ledger.note: 1807: Napoleon makes his brother Jérôme king of the new Kingdom of Westphalia at Cassel. Infobox: Treaty of Tilsit 7 July 1807; the Jérôme Bonaparte page dates his reign from 7 July 1807 (regnal table 8 July).

region.text: Göttingen and Grubenhagen with Osnabrück (the Weser department, 1807-1810)

ledger.note: 1807: Göttingen and Grubenhagen (the Leine department) and Osnabrück (the Weser department, capital Osnabrück, 1807-1810 in the page's department table) are in the kingdom from its creation. The page names Hanover among the donor lands but does not attribute these lands to it, so the counterpart is the researcher's reading (kingdom-of-hanover /ledger/2 records the same loss). Repair pass 2026-11-01: Osnabrück added because /ledger/6 below loses it in 1810 and it was never gained.

region.text: 'The counties of Mansfeld, Stolberg, Ravensberg, Rietberg and Hohnstein'

ledger.note: 1807: the county of Stolberg is among the original territories of the kingdom (page: 'The counties of Mansfeld, Stolberg, Ravensberg, Rietberg and Hohnstein'). county-of-stolberg /ledger/8 dissolves into Westphalia in 1807 (Stolberg-Wernigerode page: 'mediatised in 1807 and made part of the Kingdom of Westphalia'). This page names no month for the mediatisation (July is the kingdom's creation date) and no area; the 20 km circle at Wernigerode is a placement. Stolberg-Wernigerode was annexed by Prussia in 1813-1815 (page). Mansfeld, Ravensberg, Rietberg and Hohnstein are listed too but are not attributed to a donor here.

region.text: the whole kingdom, 'a client state of France' and 'a member of the Confederation of the Rhine'

ledger.note: 1807: Westphalia is a client state of France from its creation (page infobox: 'Client state of the French Empire'; lead: 'a client state of France in present-day Germany that existed from 1807 to 1813'; 'The state was a member of the Confederation of the Rhine'). The Westphalia page gives no month for the status. The month 11 is the author's choice, taken from the Confederation of the Rhine page's membership table ('Kingdom of Westphalia | 15 Nov 1807'), and matches first-french-empire /ledger/4; the kingdom itself was created in July 1807 (events above).

region.text: the Aller department (capital Hanover) and the coastal and northern départements Nord (capital Stade) and Niederelbe (capital Lüneburg), all held by the kingdom before the December 1810 cession

ledger.note: 1810: the Aller department (capital Hanover) appears in the page's department table for 1810-1813, and the page says that in December 1810 'the short-lived coastal and northern départements Nord ... and Niederelbe ... were ceded to the French Empire', so the kingdom held Nord and Niederelbe before that month. The page gives no date within 1810, no donor and no treaty; Hanover as donor is the researcher's reading (kingdom-of-hanover /ledger/3 records the Aller share). Repair pass 2026-11-01: the region is widened from Hanover alone to Hanover, Lüneburg and Stade so that the December 1810 loss returns land that was gained; the 1810 extent (infobox 63,652 km2) is carried by this union plus Cliopatria's 1809 shape.

1810: the Weser department (Osnabrück) is listed as lasting only 1807-1810. The page does not say where it went; the French Empire is inferred from the December 1810 cession of the neighbouring northern departments, and Cliopatria's 1811 shape no longer covers Osnabrück.

ledger.note: December 1810: 'the short-lived coastal and northern départements Nord ... and Niederelbe ... were ceded to the French Empire.' No day or treaty is named on the page; Cliopatria's shapes never include these departments.

region.text: Cassel, captured 'by surprise on the night of 28 to 29 September'

ledger.note: September 1813: the Russian general Chernyshyov seizes Cassel in a night raid and Jérôme flees; the French retake the city on 7 October.
26 October 1813: after the French defeat at Leipzig (19 October) Prussian troops occupy Westphalia; the fighting over the kingdom ends with its dissolution.

region.text: The whole kingdom: 'the kingdom was then dissolved and the status quo of 1806 was restored'

ledger.note: 26 October 1813: the Kingdom of Westphalia is dissolved after Leipzig and its lands revert to the 1806 status quo; most pass to Prussia in 1815 and Rietberg and Stolberg-Wernigerode are annexed by Prussia. Jérôme Bonaparte page: kingship ended 26 October 1813.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: Chernyshyov took Cassel on 28-29 September 1813, the French retook it on 7 October, and after Leipzig (19 October) Prussian troops occupied Westphalia on 26 October; the kingdom was dissolved and the 1806 status quo restored.
wars.note: Only the Westphalian episode is read, from the kingdom's own page; the war's own article was not opened (page budget).

notes: Cliopatria begins the kingdom in 1809; the page dates it from 1807 (new keyframe 1807-1808 uses the 1809 shape). The page gives no date or treaty for the 1810 changes: the December 1810 cession of Nord and Niederelbe is stated; the end of the Weser department (Osnabrück) in 1810 is read from the department table and its recipient (French Empire) is inferred. Cliopatria's 1809-1810 shape covers Osnabrück and Hanover but not the northern departments, so its 1810 area (43,140 km2) is below the infobox 63,652 km2. The Wikipedia Treaties of Tilsit and Confederation of the Rhine pages were not opened (budget 1-2). Gazetteer names needed: Lüneburg, Stade (places). Counterpart slug duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg is a dossier by another group (no Cliopatria row). REPAIR PASS 2026-11-01 (reviewer findings): added vassal_start 1807-11 and vassal_end 1813-10 with first-french-empire (client state; the month of the start is the author's choice from the Confederation of the Rhine page, 15 Nov 1807; the Westphalia page is silent on it); added Osnabrück to the 1807 gain from Hanover (the page lists it among the original principalities and the Weser department ran 1807-1810); added a 1807 gain from county-of-stolberg (Wernigerode circle, confidence 2); widened the 1810 gain to Hanover, Lüneburg and Stade so that the December 1810 loss of Nord and Niederelbe returns land that was gained. NOT DONE / SILENT: the page lists Goslar among the original cities without a donor, and kingdom-of-hanover /ledger/2 puts Goslar in the Hanoverian loss; no Goslar gain is recorded here because the page does not attribute it. Cross-check for eu-20 (kingdom-of-hanover): its /ledger/4 loses Nord and Niederelbe straight to first-french-empire in 1810-12, whereas this page has the kingdom hold them until it cedes them in December 1810; Hanover's loss should name kingdom-of-westphalia for 1810 and the French cession should follow. Gazetteer names still needed: Wernigerode, Lüneburg, Stade (places).
